item.content:encoded:

  • Leant on some of my CliftonStrengths™ mid-week to pull a plan out of many loose strands for a new assignment. That was particularly enjoyable.
  • Meetings are getting easier to follow, but are still incredibly hard. This is to say that grammar study is paying off, but I totally freeze up when asked questions in Japanese.
  • Got some good but hard feedback about an initiative.
  • On Friday we consumed many lemons and sang many songs.
  • Reading speed is a limiting factor in karaoke, and mine is particularly slow.
  • Oh yeah, I have a new textbook! Still bricking it.

item.dc:creator: alex
item.content:encoded:
• Busy busy busy.
  • My dentist’s uncanny mind-reading ability has struck again, and now that my teeth are fixed I have been successfully upsold on a new treatment.
  • My dermatologist finally let me graduate the big-boy skincare medication. How do I feel? Well, relieved: Six months of dry lips & skin and mood-swings were unpleasant. However it worked including strangely for my hair. I’m gonna remain on a (very) low dose.
  • Sitting in the park in Osaki is very good. Why don’t we sit in more parks?
  • Leadership training programme concluded this week. I still see room for growth in me, but I learned a lot and walk away with new connections, and new ways of thinking about motivation, growth & emotional wellbeing.
  • Team Kato!!!
  • Team drinks on Thursday were super fun and reminiscent of team nights in 2018. いい感じだったと思う.
  • Spent Friday and Saturday with visiting friends, in-between Ginza, Akasaka, Yoyogi and Omotesando. Discovered some new bars, some new coffee shops and talked a lot about eastern european…

item.dc:creator: alex
item.content:encoded:
• How do I describe this week?

  • Well, I have been feeling a bit burned out from studying and fitness, as well as reckoning with other some small things over the week. So in an act of kindness to myself I decided to slow down on a few fronts for the week.

  • Opened the week with the annual health-check, and I am pleased to report that I beat my score from last year (not deliberately). This was also a much more pleasant experience than last year: I guess afternoons are less popular?

    • Unfortunately this somehow resulted in a nasty friction burn. If you're wondering what the bandages are for: It's that.

  • I then proceeded to do my best to undo that high-score over the week’s dinners. It’s OK: This was entirely deliberate and I enjoyed each and every conversation.

  • Discovered an unpatched technique on the way.

  • And got some useful input on a problem.

item.title: Get with the #times
item.description: One of the first things I was surprised by working in technology in Japan was the prevalence of “#times channels”. Channels named after individuals in which they (and others) will post more-or-less whatever they like…
item.dc:creator: alex
item.content:encoded:
One of the first things I was surprised by working in technology in Japan was the prevalence of “#times channels”. Channels named after individuals in which they (and others) will post more-or-less whatever they like.

Reader, I have come to really love them, and I think you might too.

OK I'll bite, what is a #times channel?

Times channels are personal channels (on Slack, but sometimes in Discord or other systems), and they are somewhere between a personal log, water-cooler chat and a back channel. Nobody is obliged to read them and nothing official happens in them, yet they weave together to form a useful social fabric.

The first times channel was probably #times_suin, and it was created as a complement to daily reporting: The cadence of daily reports (日報) meant that hours spent on a problem would not be visible to the colleagues and experts who might be able to help, and so #times_suin was created as an experimental "minute report" (分報) to allow for in-the-minute interventions.

item.dc:creator: alex
item.content:encoded:
• Gosh, the weather hasn’t been great. A record number of days WFH this week.
  • To make WFH more fun, I procured a HHKB Studio: It is great, genuinely the best keyboard I have ever used. I ported the POK3R’s keymap and now I have full muscle memory from my UK daily driver.
  • Better discipline is paying off, even if I’m finding having more unplanned free time a bit boring. I think it’s yielding dividends though: I am in the middle of learning a lesson!
  • Mortified by something I did on Tuesday. A small faux-pas. Positively mortified reader.
  • Put together and presented a new process at an all-hands which I’m quite happy with. Reception was good, I hope that it goes as smoothly as the kick-off!
  • I skipped a day of Japanese revision on Friday and woke up to 3 hours worth of reviews on Saturday morning. That was not fun.
  • Testing a few new ideas in my Kanji revision, to both explore/prioritise how I learn kanji, and to also help me practice self-talk. I'm on track for December, just about, and…

item.dc:creator: alex
item.content:encoded:
• Many meetings and events at work this week, including an interesting leadership training day where I learned how personal values manifest in decision-making. I wish I saw this years ago.
  • I put up the fans I picked up from this & last years’ Azabu festival in my entrance hall and it’s a nice little touch that I absolutely love, as well as a reminder of two very different summers.
  • Pizza dinner plus a walk to Osaki was a real highlight. Probably the best pizza I have had in Japan, and the first that I was super impressed by.
  • Finally attempted a run to work. It’s possible, just about. Running outside is highlighting just how ineffective treadmill running is, because where my recovery is great on a treadmill, it’s much harder outside. I’m also worse at regulating my speed. Tackling my inner sprinter is going to be important if I want to do distance seriously.
  • Kuro Sushi is cute, and absurdly cheap. More dinners like these, please?

  • On Monday JLPT exam applications opened, and after much rigmarole I am now signed up. Positively bricking it!
  • Last week’s festival food did not sit right with me, and long story short, an unsettled stomach led me to an useful discovery: Calorie Mate. It’s, uh, surprisingly good? And because each piece is exactly 100 calories it is a very easy way of nudging out of a calorie deficit. I will be having this stuff again.
  • Thursday is a farewell-for-now party for a friend under similar circumstances to my move to Bulgaria: I’m delighted but it’s still bittersweet. The restaurant has amazing chicken, and I regret not asking for more. I pass on karaoke this time.

item.dc:creator: alex
item.content:encoded:
• Reader, I have a new room-mate. A jumping spider. It is tiny, seems friendly and since I have no idea where it came from, I guess it just lives here now.
  • No lunches this week. I also bruised my ego a little bit. Let’s do better next week, eh?
  • Sat a “surprise” mock Japanese exam. I passed, and lost the most my marks in a section with a type of question I had never seen before. Were I to sit this exam again I would now get a much better score.
  • Went to the second session of leadership training. It went to a new place for such programmes: Looking inwards and at inner personal growth. This is very apt timing and sparked good conversation afterwards, and at least one book loan!
  • Side-quest alert: Made a little NFC reader Chrome Extension for an event at work. NFC readers are mostly a solved problem and the most difficult part was getting the reviews and permissions to ship it. This was fun, I enjoy these little side-quests. I hope it gets some use.
